episodes.193555: Strong to severe storms formed out ahead of an approaching cold front moving in from western Montana.
episodes.193617: Monsoon storms across the West Mesa west of Albuquerque sent a strong outflow boundary through town. This outflow boundary ended up producing a 59 mph wind gust at the Albuquerque Sunport.
episodes.193627: A supercell formed along the Canadian border in the afternoon and moved across far northeastern Montana.  Later at night a large supercell formed in Garfield County and moved across the Dry Arm of Fort Peck Lake causing extensive damage to Rock Creek Marina.  This supercell eventually evolved into a line of storms and moved across northeast Montana on the morning of the 25th before weakening and exiting the area before sunrise.
episodes.194117: A surface low meandered offshore of the NE FL coastal along a stalled front. Passing upper-level short wave trough energy, high moisture and slow storm motion produced locally heavy rainfall and pulse strong storms with wet downbursts in resultant storms. Storms impacted coastal areas in the morning, then with diurnal heating shift inland.
episodes.194247: Scattered storms produced severe outflow winds over north central Kansas during the early morning on 08/24.
episodes.194252: An anomalously strong upper level trough was set up just off the west coast, which resulted in a strong belt of mid level southerly flow across Southwest through North-central Montana. Synoptic winds were already breezy from the south, allowing thunderstorms to easily produce strong wind gusts given inverted-V soundings. Wind gusts in excess of 80 mph were observed on this day as a line of gusty outflow spread northward over the plains.||A High Wind Warning was also issued for Southwest Montana this day, though no strong synoptic gusts were observed.

episodes.195000: Thunderstorms developed on the warm, moist side of a stationary front. Some of these storms produced damaging wind gusts.
episodes.195345: Isolated severe thunderstorms produced wind damage mainly across portions of Callahan and Taylor counties.
episodes.195431: Above-normal moisture associated with a tropical wave combined with increased instability due to an upper-level trough and enhanced by local effects and a sea breeze promoted thunderstorm formation across PR's interior and western sections, triggering flooding and mudslides.
episodes.195491: With deep monsoonal moisture in place, as well as around 1000 J/kg of instability and some bulk shear aloft, widespread strong to severe thunderstorms formed across the Four Corners region. This resulted in multiple severe threats in eastern Utah, but was limited to heavier rain, non-severe hail, and some severe wind gusts in southwest Colorado.
episodes.195643: Light winds and deep tropical moisture were amongst some of the environmental ingredients that supported the potential for waterspouts on August 24. There was at least one report of a waterspout sighting just of the coast of South Padre Island the morning of August 24th.
episodes.195825: An early season cold front from a low pressure system moving across Nevada increased the chance for scattered showers that initiated during the early morning hours of August 25th. The heaviest showers were projected to stay mostly north of I-80 with a 50-60% chance of showers along the Sierra crest that extended south to Mammoth Lakes. There was also a 20-30% chance of thunderstorms as well. Some showers along the Sierra above 9000' had the potential to bring a dusting of snow.

episodes.196146: There were gusty winds for different parts of Utah and flash flooding in southern Utah.
episodes.196164: Slow moving, heavy rain showers moved over the the higher terrain near Wenatchee. Rain amounts ranged from 0.4 to 0.6 of an inch from 1700-2000 PST. The runoff was funneled through the canyons and caused flash flooding for parts of Western Wenatchee.
episodes.196239: Several gale-force wind gusts were observed over the Florida Keys coastal waters as a tropical wave moved westward.
episodes.196297: Showers resulted in an observed funnel cloud close to the Columbia River in Vancouver, WA. The funnel cloud was observed from Portland, Oregon as well as from Vancouver, WA.

No reports of damage or injury were received in association with this gust.
